fatal.subject: lem-local-boundedness-of-separately-holomorphic-functions
fatal.note: The repaired Hartogs-coefficient argument still cited the log-modulus theorem without its non-identically-zero hypothesis: [L6] omitted that clause and step 5.1 applied it to coefficient functions c_alpha that could vanish identically. 6c repaired the citation and restricted the subharmonic family to c_alpha not identically zero.

fatal.subject: lem-local-boundedness-of-separately-holomorphic-functions
fatal.note: Step 5.1 and the start of step 7.1 treated u_alpha = |alpha|^{-1} log|c_alpha| as a subharmonic family for every nonzero multi-index, but def-plane-subharmonic-function excludes functions that are identically -infinity on a component. When c_alpha is identically zero, u_alpha is identically -infinity and the cited definition does not apply. 6c repaired the proof by separating the c_alpha ≡ 0 case and enumerating only the nonzero coefficient functions.

fatal.subject: lem-local-boundedness-of-separately-holomorphic-functions
fatal.note: Step 7.1 invoked plane local integrability on the coefficient family before proving that every member of that family satisfied the subharmonic definition. The local-integrability citation becomes licensed only after the family is restricted to c_alpha not identically zero.

fatal.subject: lem-local-boundedness-of-separately-holomorphic-functions
fatal.note: The Fatou step in 7.1 was written for the same overbroad family of potential coefficient functions. Once the proof separates c_alpha ≡ 0 from the genuine subharmonic family, the nonpositive functions w_j are locally integrable and Fatou applies as cited.

fatal.subject: thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign
fatal.note: The old step 2.1 inferred |q_n(x)|≤g(x) from separate mean-value bounds on the real and imaginary parts of the complex quotient, which yields at best a √2-type estimate and does not prove the claimed domination. Alpha repaired the theorem by rotating q_n(x) with α=overline{q_n(x)}/|q_n(x)| and applying the real mean value theorem to Re(α f(x,·)).

fatal.subject: lem-boundary-point-whose-complementary-component-contains-another-point-is-regular
fatal.note: The proof falsely asserted that the Mobius image T(Omega) is bounded; 6b removed that claim and kept only the properties actually used in the logarithmic peak-function construction.

fatal.subject: thm-upper-envelope-theorem-for-plane-subharmonic-functions
fatal.note: The proof falsely claimed that local boundedness above forces pointwise finiteness on compact sets; 6b rewrote the step to use only the upper-bound and non-identically-minus-infinity obligations that are actually true.
